newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Anderton sees NZ First, Nats as most compatible.
newsitem.headline: Anderton sees NZ First, Nats as most compatible.

text.p: Alliance leader Jim Anderton said on Wednesday economic nationalist New Zealand First and the ruling National Party "are the most likely compatible coalition partners after the election".
"If you look at the policy mix now (of New Zealand First) it is almost compatible without blinking an eye-lid with National," Anderton said in a radio interview.
He said when former National MP Michael Laws joined the New Zealand First Party earlier this year it was a watershed. He said Laws' policy work began moving it towards National's position.
New Zealand First leader Winston Peters has kept his coalition options open.
While criticising Labour's fiscal policy, lack of savings strategy and "excessive regard for trade union powers" he has said its social policy is more acceptable than National's.

In Monday night's TV1 leaders debate and in recent radio interviews Prime Minister Jim Bolger has appeared to hold out an olive branch to New Zealand First saying its economic policies are more responsible than those of Labour and the Alliance.

On the basis of current polling a deal between the main opposition Labour Party and New Zealand First with the support of the Alliance on confidence issues is seen as the most likely government after the October 12 election.
Together they are polling 52 percent support against 35 percent for National.
